title: Laredo's Public Art Takes Shape: 99 Community Designs, 52 From Students, Unveiled Starting This Month

content:
Laredo's Public Art Program is moving from planning to installation — and the city's streets, libraries and public spaces are about to become the canvas.

The city has selected 99 community-created concepts for development, including 52 designs contributed by local students, according to reporting in the Laredo Morning Times summarized by Wisevoter. The city expects a series of project unveilings across the area between November 2026 and March 2027.

The program is funded by dedicating 2% of construction costs from eligible capital improvement projects to art — works that include ground murals, library art and mini-gallery posts. City officials surveyed more than 180 local artists and engaged with 184 workshop attendees to choose the final designs from a pool of 290 total submissions.

Current project expenditures are trending 46% below the projected budget, according to the same reporting — a notable detail for a program built on public construction dollars.

The program itself was established in 2019, and officials approved its first annual plan in October 2025. Not everything moves at once: the Texas Department of Transportation is conducting a safety assessment that has paused installation of specific control-cabinet murals.

What comes next is visible and local: ground murals and library installations appearing across the city over the next several months, giving students and community artists high-visibility platforms for their work — public art made by the community, for the community, in the places it walks every day.

Sources:

  • Wisevoter, including information reported by Laredo Morning Times — Laredo Transitions Public Art Program to Installation (October 26, 2026)
